event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: WST’s 2023 Form 10-K situates COVID-19 as an ongoing, multi-dimensional risk that is still very fresh (within three years of the March 2020 WHO declaration).  The filing describes both realised impacts—global supply-chain breakdowns, labour-market disruptions, demand volatility—and a wide set of forward-looking exposures: renewed lockdowns, variant waves, and distribution bottlenecks that could ‘significantly impact’ production.  Several passages explicitly tie the pandemic to adverse effects on results of operations, financial condition, manufacturing continuity and talent retention, demonstrating management’s recognition of material risk.  Although the company notes certain mitigants (continued plant operations, monitoring efforts, easing restrictions), these are outweighed by acknowledgements of uncertainty and the possibility of significant future disruption.  Given the recency of the event, the specificity of the cited operational pinch-points (supply chain, labour, distribution channels) and the direct link to financial performance, the aggregate COVID-19 risk profile is assessed as elevated-to-high.  Time-decay does not materially diminish severity because the pandemic remains within the 0-3-year “recent” window, so individual snippet scores can legitimately fall in the upper range unless materially offset by mitigation language.

evidence_list.snippet: Our results of operations and financial condition may be adversely affected by the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and other public health epidemics.

components.reason: Directly links ongoing COVID-19 pandemic to potential adverse impact on results and financial condition.
Uses explicit adverse-impact wording ('may be adversely affected').
Event is recent (0-3 yrs), amplifying relevance.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Clear statement of potential material harm from a very recent event; moderately strong but generic, so scored 5.

evidence_list.snippet: Our operations expose us to risks associated with a pandemic, or outbreak of contagious diseases in the human population, including the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Acknowledges operational exposure to pandemic risk, specifically naming COVID-19.
Statement is generic with no quantified or detailed impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic risk acknowledgement with little detail; minimal severity after deduction for vagueness.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has negatively impacted the global economy, disrupted consumer spending and global supply chains, disrupted the labor market, created significant volatility and disruption of financial markets and has resulted in governments around the world implementing stringent measures to help control the spread of the virus.

components.reason: States that COVID-19 has already caused negative impacts (realised, not just potential).
Enumerates specific operational pinch-points (consumer spending, supply chains, labor).
Uses strong severity language ('negatively impacted', 'significant volatility').
Event is within 0-3 years (high relevance).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highly specific, multi-faceted realised impacts linked to recent event justify a near-maximum score.

evidence_list.snippet: We are subject to risks associated with public health crises, such as pandemics and epidemics, including the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Mentions COVID-19 explicitly as a risk factor.
Very broad, boiler-plate wording dilutes severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad boiler-plate reference provides weak evidence; net score kept low.

evidence_list.snippet: The functioning of our manufacturing and distribution assets and systems could be disrupted for reasons either within or beyond our control, including, without limitation: extreme weather, water scarcity and other longer-term climatic changes; natural or man-made disasters; pandemic; war; accidental damage; disruption to the supply of material or services; product quality and safety issues; systems failure; workforce actions; or environmental matters.

components.reason: Lists 'pandemic' as a cause of manufacturing/distribution disruption.
Pandemic reference is buried among many other hazards, reducing specificity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Pandemic included but diluted in a long hazard list; results in low severity.

evidence_list.snippet: While many countries around the world have removed or reduced the restrictions taken in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, the emergence of new variants of the SARS-CoV-2 virus may result in new governmental lockdowns, quarantine requirements or other restrictions to slow the spread of the virus.

components.reason: Highlights possibility of renewed lockdowns and other restrictive measures affecting operations.
Acknowledges some mitigation (restrictions removed/reduced).
Forward-looking risk tied to variants keeps event relevance high.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Balances new-variant risk (+) against easing restrictions (-); yields modest score.

evidence_list.snippet: The scope and duration of any future public health crisis, including the potential emergence of new variants of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, the pace at which government restrictions, including, but not limited to, quarantines, “shelter in place” and “stay at home” order, travel restrictions and other similar measures, are imposed and lifted, the scope of additional actions taken to mitigate the spread of disease, global vaccination and booster rates, may significantly impact our production throughout the supply chain and constrict distribution channels.

components.reason: Connects pandemic dynamics directly to production and supply-chain impact.
Uses strong severity phrase ('may significantly impact').
References new variants and fluctuating restrictions, indicating ongoing risk.
Mentions constriction of distribution channels (additional operational risk).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Detailed operational exposure with strong wording and multiple risk vectors merits high score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: Our production facilities continue to operate as they had prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, other than for enhanced safety measures intended to prevent the spread of the virus and higher levels of production at certain plant locations to meet additional customer demand.

components.reason: Indicates continuity of operations and even higher production (mitigating factor).
Mentions COVID-19 context, showing monitoring.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Net effect is mitigating; after deductions, snippet conveys no incremental pandemic risk.

evidence_list.snippet: Competition for experienced employees, particularly for persons with specialized skills, can be intense and has intensified following the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Explicitly links pandemic to heightened labour-market pressure.
Labour shortages can directly affect operations and capacity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows a concrete pandemic-driven labour risk; substantial but not quantified, giving a mid-level score.

evidence_list.snippet: West has been actively monitoring the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic globally.

components.reason: Shows management awareness and monitoring (partly mitigating).
Confirms pandemic remains a salient factor prompting corporate oversight.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Purely a monitoring statement; risk impact effectively neutral after mitigation.
